title: Small ordinary model diagrams rectify coherent diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, the ordinary nerve, coherent functor categories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and a complete and cocomplete ordinary category $\mathcal M$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences: $W$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of two mutually characterized diagonal-lifting classes and a factorization of every arrow into its left and right classes. For a relative ordinary category $(\mathcal A,V)$, write $q_{\mathcal A}:N(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A[V^{-1}]_\infty$ for a universal homotopy coherent localization: restriction into every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ identifies the entire functor quasicategory out of the target with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathcal A),\mathcal E)$ on functors inverting $V$. The localization universes may be enlarged beyond $\mathcal U$.

For every $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $I$, put $W_I=\{a:D\to E\mid a_i\in W\text{ for every }i\in I\}$. Evaluation and $q_{\mathcal M}$ induce an equivalence of infinity categories
$$\Theta_I:\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M)[W_I^{-1}]_\infty\xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty).$$
Its composite with $q_{\mathcal M^I}$ is coherently naturally equivalent to $D\mapsto q_{\mathcal M}\circ N(D)$, including the corresponding transformations. The comparisons commute coherently with restriction along functors of small indexing categories. In particular they identify the localized constant-diagram functor with the coherent constant-diagram functor. Neither simplicial enrichment, combinatoriality, properness, objectwise cofibrancy, nor a model structure on $\mathcal M^I$ is assumed.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026 revision: Theorem 7.9.8, printed pp. 409-412, applied to the nerve of an ordinary bicomplete model category; Remark 7.9.7 supplies heredity from closure of sequential (trivial) cofibrations, while the dual of Definition 7.7.2 is satisfied by coproduct lifting in a bicomplete model category; Proposition 7.7.4 records the resulting localized (co)completeness. The comparison is induced by evaluation, so restriction and constants agree. Read online, not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent rectification theorem.

proof.text: Let $0$ be an initial object, let $\mathcal M_c$ be the full subcategory of objects $X$ with $0\to X\in C$ (the cofibrant objects), and write $\iota:\mathcal M_c\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$ for inclusion. Work in a common larger universe containing all categories and their mapping spaces; all colimits asserted below remain $\mathcal U$-small. Choose the functorial factorization of $0\to X$ into $0\to QX$ in $C$ and $e_X:QX\to X$ in $F\cap W$. It gives a functor $Q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M_c$ and a natural weak equivalence $e:\iota Q\to\mathrm{id}$. Naturality and two-out-of-three imply that $Q$ preserves weak equivalences. On $\mathcal M_c$ the same $e$ has both endpoints in $\mathcal M_c$, so $Q\iota\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M_c}$ is also a natural weak equivalence. Apply this pointwise to strict diagrams. The entire-functor-category localization property descends these functors and transformations; their components become equivalences, hence they are coherent natural equivalences. Thus it suffices to compare $\mathcal A=N(\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c))[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$ with $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal B)$, where $\mathcal B=N(\mathcal M_c)[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$. This reduction constructs quasi-inverses and does not assume a model structure on $\mathcal M^I$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 7.9.8, reduction to cofibrant objects after (7.9.8.2); here implemented directly using the assumed functorial model factorization.

proof.text: Verify the hypotheses of [lem-coef-cocomplete-cofibration-localization] for $\mathcal M_c$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c)$ with pointwise cofibrations and weak equivalences. Isomorphisms have both diagonal lifting properties and hence belong to $C\cap W$ and $F\cap W$. The lifting-class closure gives identities, composition, retracts and pushout closure for $C$ and $C\cap W$. Weak equivalences in each diagram category are closed under composition and retracts and satisfy two-out-of-three because evaluation sends a composite or an arrow-retract diagram to the corresponding diagram in $\mathcal M$. Factorizations starting at a cofibrant object have cofibrant middle object. For diagram arrows, applying the functorial factorization in $\mathcal M$ componentwise gives a natural factorization, and pushouts and coproducts are formed pointwise. A coproduct of left-lifting maps has the same lifting property: restrict a lifting square to each summand, choose its lift, and assemble the lifts. In particular coproducts of cofibrant objects are cofibrant. For a pushout along a cofibration between cofibrant objects, the other target is cofibrant because its initial map followed by the pushed-out cofibration is a cofibration. These checks give all the hypotheses of the cited cocompletion lemma without diagram fibrations. It follows that $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ admit all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and their localization functors preserve initial objects, coproducts and cofibration pushouts. The relative co-Yoneda lemma gives pointwise colimits in $\mathcal P$. The strict diagram functor $D\mapsto q\circ N(D)$ inverts $W_I$, preserves those initial objects, coproducts and cofibration pushouts pointwise, and therefore descends by the cocompletion lemma to a colimit-preserving functor $\Theta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P$.

source.place: Dual of Definition 7.7.2, Proposition 7.7.4 and Theorem 7.7.9; Theorem 7.9.8, (7.9.8.1)-(7.9.8.2).

proof.text: For each $i$, form the strict free diagram $E_iX(j)=\coprod_{\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)}X$. The ordinary adjunction $E_i\dashv\operatorname{ev}_i$ is explicit: a transformation $E_iX\to D$ is determined by its map $X\to D(i)$ on the identity summand; conversely use $D(u)$ on the $u:i\to j$ summand. Both functors preserve weak equivalences on cofibrant objects. For $E_i$, this follows from Brown split factorizations: for any family of weak equivalences $f$, write $f=pi$ and $ps=1$ with $p$ trivial fibrations and $i,s$ cofibrations. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Their coproducts are trivial cofibrations by the summand lifting argument; $(\coprod p)(\coprod s)=1$ then makes $\coprod p$, and finally $\coprod f$, weak equivalences. Descend the two relative functors and the ordinary unit and counit via the full functor-category localization property. The triangle identities descend too, since restriction is fully faithful, giving $E_i^L\dashv\operatorname{ev}_i^L$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(E_i^Lx,D)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,D(i))$. Adjunction and the colimit mapping-space property imply $E_i^L$ preserves small colimits: mapping out of $E_i^L\operatorname{colim}x_k$ is the limit of the maps out of $E_i^Lx_k$. Finite-product preservation of localization descends the whole bifunctor $N(I)^{\mathrm{op}}\times N(\mathcal M_c)\to\mathcal A$ to $T:N(I)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. Preservation of coproducts by $q$ identifies $\Theta T(i,x)$ with the coherent free diagram $i!x$, including its maps in both variables.

source.place: Theorem 7.9.8, (7.9.8.3)-(7.9.8.9); Proposition 7.1.14 for descending adjunctions, written out using the full localization property.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-coherent-diagram-coyoneda] to $T$ to obtain a colimit-preserving $H:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$ with $H(i!x)\simeq E_i^Lx$. The colimit-preserving functors $\Theta H$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P}$ agree coherently on the free bifunctor, hence the entire-functor-category extension equivalence gives a natural equivalence $\Theta H\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P}$. For $F\in\mathcal P$ and $D\in\mathcal A$, take the canonical free-diagram presentation of $F$ on the small final $K_F$ provided by the same lemma. The colimit mapping property and the adjunction of step 3 give, naturally in $F,D$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(HF,D)\simeq\lim_{K_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(E_i^Lx,D)\simeq\lim_{K_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,D(i))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(F,\Theta D).$$
The pointwise representability criterion promotes this bifunctor equivalence to $H\dashv\Theta$ with coherent unit and counit. On every free diagram its unit is an equivalence, since the displayed bifunctor equivalence restricts to the evaluation adjunction in step 3. Both $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P}$ and $\Theta H$ preserve small colimits. The free-diagram presentation then makes the unit an equivalence on every $F$, retaining coherent transformations. All colimits in this calculation are on $K_F$, never on an unrestricted large slice.

source.place: Theorem 7.9.8, (7.9.8.6), (7.9.8.9)-(7.9.8.10) and the mapping-space calculation on printed pp. 410-411.

proof.text: Let $\epsilon:H\Theta\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ be that adjunction's counit. Write $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P}\to\Theta H$ for the unit, which step 4 proved invertible. For $F=i!x$, the triangle identity is $\epsilon_{HF}\circ H(\eta_F)=1_{HF}$. Since $H(\eta_F)$ is an equivalence, this identity makes $\epsilon_{HF}$ its inverse. The coherent free-diagram identification supplies an equivalence $a:H(i!x)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_i^Lx$. Naturality gives $\epsilon_{E_i^Lx}\circ H\Theta(a)=a\circ\epsilon_{H(i!x)}$. Both $H\Theta(a)$ and the right-hand composite are equivalences, so $\epsilon_{E_i^Lx}$ is an equivalence. The full replete subcategory of $\mathcal A$ on objects where $\epsilon$ is an equivalence is closed under small colimits: both $H\Theta$ and the identity preserve them, and a colimit functor takes equivalences of coherent diagrams to equivalences. The free strict diagram generation lemma applies, with the model hypotheses unchanged and the colimits supplied in step 2, so this subcategory is all of $\mathcal A$. Componentwise equivalence of transformations makes both the unit and counit coherent natural equivalences. Thus $H$ is a quasi-inverse of $\Theta$, proving the comparison on objects and all mapping spaces.

source.place: The free-diagram generation part of Theorem 7.9.8, (7.9.8.11)-(7.9.8.14), printed pp. 411-412; the counit argument packages that generation into the equivalence proof.

proof.text: Transfer the comparison back through the pointwise cofibrant-replacement equivalences of step 1. Before localization, its underlying bifunctor is evaluation followed by $q_{\mathcal M}$; the natural transformation $Q D\to D$ identifies the transferred functor with $D\mapsto q_{\mathcal M}\circ N(D)$. The entire-functor-category localization property extends this identification on objects, transformations and all higher simplices. For $v:J\to I$, the prelocalization evaluation bifunctors commute strictly with restriction $v^*$; their equality, and the equalities for composite restrictions and identity restrictions, descend through the same fully faithful restriction equivalences. This provides the requested coherent restriction compatibility. Taking $I\to *$ gives constant diagrams. For $I=\varnothing$ both categories are terminal, and the generation argument uses the empty colimit; for $I=*$ the comparison is the identity localization. Thus no enrichment, combinatoriality, properness or diagram model structure has entered the proof.

source.place: The canonical evaluation comparison (7.9.8.1)-(7.9.8.2) and Remark 7.9.10; restriction and constant compatibility follow from its full coherent localization property.
